The instruction states only the perceived symptom: the field reporting on a draft's
validation carries the platform's generic state wording. It names no file, no component,
no mechanism and no target wording, so the screenshot is the only reliable trail to which
field of which panel is at fault — the agent must read the rendered value next to its
label to see that a work state is being presented under the wording the platform reserves
for the draft workflow status.

The fix is not a one-line edit. The block that renders that field is shared with a second
screen, where the generic wording is correct, so changing the label in place regresses the
other call site. The agent has to discover that the block is shared and turn the label into

in-place rename and needed a code review before a second commit made the label dynamic.

ConnectorWorkLine.tsx; commit 06e2a2a introduces the statusLabel prop and reverts it. The
task's p2p guards would reject dfd6074, since it relabels the connectors screen too.)

MEASURED — the hardening above did NOT hold up, across TWO trials on
claude-code @ anthropic/claude-opus-4-8, each scoring reward 1.0 on its FIRST attempt
with f2p 4/4 and p2p 6/6. QC records this as trial_not_hard_enough.

  trial 2 (instruction.md rewritten vaguer: user-voice report, no field enumeration,

  - The image IS load-bearing, and worked as designed. In BOTH trials the agent's first
    action was reading bug_screenshot_1.png, and its next was grepping for field labels
    it read OFF that screenshot ("Operations Completed", "Work Start Time", ...) to

    them from it changed nothing. This is strong evidence that

    every ConnectorWorkLine call site BEFORE editing, found DraftRoot.tsx, and went
    straight to the per-call-site fix; trial 2 also read ConnectorWorks.tsx first. The
    mistake that got past human code review was not a mistake for this model.

Conclusion: the difficulty is real for a human reviewer but not for a frontier model.
The target is one string literal, reachable in one grep hop from the labels visible in
the poster, and the f2p contract constrains only that the new label matches /validation/i
and differs from the generic word — so there is no wording to guess. Vaguer prose can
hide WHERE to look; it cannot make a two-line fix demanding. Raising the difficulty
means changing what is asked, not tightening the tests or the instruction. difficulty is
left at "medium" pending that decision, and this note is the standing caveat.

  "Draft validation work status (p2p guards) > still shows the work state itself in both contexts",
  "Draft validation work status (p2p guards) > still shows the name, timings and counters of the draft validation work",
  "Draft validation work status (p2p guards) > renders one generic work line per work of the connectors screen",
]
